case_a.site_type: Multi-page company website, not a conversion landing page. Global navigation must open independent pages. It must not scroll to sections on the homepage.

routes.purpose: Home: the brand's first impression, a short summary of each topic and links to the inner pages. It should not repeat their full content.
Collections index: lets visitors find, scan and compare collections. Content must be specific to this page, with a next step toward enquiry.
Only if the user supplies real categories: details and context for each category, a route back to the index and an enquiry action. Otherwise leave out and record as a content gap.
Quality page with its own explanation and evidence. Use only facts the user supplies. Mark any placeholder claims as assumptions, never as guarantees.
Contact page with a clear enquiry task. If the header CTA also goes here, this page must support that CTA's specific task.

case_a.reference_role: The cinematic mockup is visual evidence only: mood, imagery treatment, typography character and focal composition. These qualities may carry over. It does not decide the site structure: the user's current request for a complete website overrides its single-page form. The two anchor-based builds stay as unchanged past deliveries. They are not a base to be patched toward a pass.
header_review: Inspect at actual display size on desktop, at an intermediate width (e.g. 1024px) and on a narrow phone. Do not judge from thumbnails.
Wordmark is legible, with baseline alignment shared across the brand, labels and CTA. Label size stays readable and is never shrunk to keep the desktop layout.
Switch to compact navigation before the wordmark, links and CTA collide or wrap.
There is a clear CTA hierarchy and the header stands apart from the hero imagery.
Hover, focus and pressed states are visible. Each inner page shows a current-page indicator, and category pages mark Collections as current.
Use a short set of page links and one useful CTA. Do not invent a mega menu, search or language selector without a content need.
The mobile menu keeps every destination and shows the current page. Its open and closed states are specified. A modal drawer needs focus management and a way to dismiss it.
Use links for destinations and buttons for actions.

Report each detail defect with the viewport, the observed problem, its cause from source or computed layout, the intended treatment and the checks it affects. Fix it across the whole component family (icons, rules, captions, footer).
Check the first viewport, typography wrapping with the longest real labels, a shared grid, image crops that keep detail, and distinct layouts for story, index and form instead of repeated hero cards.
verification: On Home, clicking Collections, Quality and Contact each opens /collections/, /quality/ and /contact/ with a real URL change and content specific to that page.
Global navigation works from an inner page: from /contact/ click Quality, and from /quality/ click Collections. The current-page indicator updates each time.
Each route loads directly by URL, survives a refresh, and Back/Forward returns to the right page and state.
Header links contain no #hash targets. Empty wrappers around homepage excerpts fail.
Mobile: on a narrow phone, open the menu, go to each page, then check that the menu closes and the current page is shown. Repeat at an intermediate width.
Keyboard: Tab through the header and menu with visible focus. Enter activates links. Dismiss the menu and check where focus returns.
The Contact primary action gives honest feedback, with no fake success. Check responsive composition at every agreed viewport.
Capture full-size screenshots. Record any check that could not run (e.g. no browser tool) as not run. Report functional pass/fail, visual judgement and user acceptance separately.
unknowns: Real collection names and categories, and product facts
Contact details and enquiry handling (backend, or mailto)
Which header and detail issues disappointed the user (e.g. size, legibility, CTA, contrast)
Whether other pages (e.g. About) are wanted. Ask one focused question only if the answer changes the experience.

case_b.site_type: One-page event campaign landing page, as the user explicitly requested.
case_b.navigation: Overview, Schedule, FAQ and Register are intentional in-page anchors (#overview, #schedule, #faq, #register). Clicking one scrolls to its section on the same page. Each target clears the fixed header, and the hash updates so the link can be shared and Back works. Keyboard focus moves to the target section. An optional active-section indicator can show the current section. The mobile menu closes after a selection. Register leads to a real registration action with honest feedback. Verify each anchor lands correctly on desktop and phone, and verify keyboard use.
case_b.scope_policy: Keep the one-page scope. Do not add separate routes or apply case A's multi-page contract. Only an explicit user request changes the scope.

case_c.cleanup: Stop only the server process, or process group, that the worker started, using the handle it kept. Wait for it to exit, confirm the exit and record the code, then release its port. Never use broad pkill -f or kill by matching the shared server command, because that could stop the other user's preview. If ownership of a process is not established, leave it running and report it.
case_c.failure_reporting: Check each native command's exit status immediately, and do not let a grep pipeline hide it. Record the exit code and an excerpt from stderr, keep raw logs local and private, and write evidence to fresh paths without overwriting. Report a failed worker or server even if another one succeeded, and say which checks did not run.

case_d.historical_verification: Keep the 93/100 score with its original scope: reference fidelity for a single-page demo, under that rubric and its limitations. It is evidence about that one check. It does not show the website is ready and is not a baseline for the new multi-page scope. Functional verification of the new standalone-page scope has not been done.
case_d.current_acceptance: Design acceptance is open, because the user explicitly rejected the design. The clarified standalone-page requirements need a new contract and a new scoring protocol. Passing automated checks would not close user acceptance.
